thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 streaming latency > 30s for dedicated pools in us-west-2. SLO breach triggered. auto-page to #incidents and paging list.

samir_oncall: picking this up — putting RTP on-call in the thread. initial triage in progress.

maria_sre: saw the same. p95 ~ 5.8s, p99 ~ 38s for streaming endpoints. non-streaming generation p99 ~ 12s. queue depth on several dedicated pools spiked to 450 (capacity 256).

ajay_runtime: early hypothesis: autoscaler failed to add new slots; handshake timeouts between orchestrator and dedicated node agents increased. I'm seeing repeated `handshake rejected: time drift` logs.

nora_prodeng: whoa. time drift? any recent rolling restart or NTP changes in the fleet?

samir_oncall: customers affected: 3 tier-2 customers in us-west-2 (IDs: cust-338, cust-551, cust-772). customer-ops notified firstreach.

customer-ops: we've opened tickets for cust-338 and cust-551. raising visibility. they report long streaming stalls and spinner behaviour in product.

ajay_runtime: posting relevant logs:```
2026-03-15T10:03:12Z agent[pool-12]: handshake: incoming ts=1712345678 local_ts=1712345650 drift=28s -> rejected
2026-03-15T10:03:13Z autoscaler: pool add attempt failed: handshake rejected
2026-03-15T10:03:14Z runtime: request queued, len=432
```

maria_sre: interesting. drift ~28s is above our 10s threshold. Could be NTP config drift on new nodes or a clock skew bug after an infra image change. any recent AMI/instance config flips?

nora_prodeng: we rolled a kernel param change in us-west-2 image last night to address ephemeral devs. ops said nothing about ntp. I'll check infra release notes.

samir_oncall: immediate mitigation options? can we temporarily relax handshake drift threshold to allow scaling?

ajay_runtime: we can toggle the handshake threshold from 10s -> 60s via feature flag in control plane, but that opens risk if clocks are wildly different. however for emergency it should let autoscaler add nodes and drain queue.

maria_sre: Suggest two-step: 1) manual scale up to add capacity (force new nodes) so requests stop queuing; 2) enable relaxed handshake threshold as fallback to let autoscaler continue. Manual scale first because flag rollout takes ~2 mins.

samir_oncall: manual scale up started: `infra-scale --pool=dedicated-usw2-hotshot --count+20`

deploy-bot: deploy started by samir_oncall at 2026-03-15T10:07:02Z — adding 20 nodes to pool.

ajay_runtime: I'm going to flip the handshake threshold flag now to 60s for us-west-2 (namespaced config). Doing it in 3...2...1.

ajay_runtime: Done. autoscaler logs now show `handshake accepted` for new agents. autoscaler resumed provisioning.

maria_sre: p95/p99 are moving: p95 -> 3.2s, p99 -> 12s; queue depth dropping from 432 -> 110 in the next minute. streaming stalls still present for some inflight sessions (some streams hit tokenization stalls).

nora_prodeng: checking node images — infra did flip a timezone/clock package update in the us-west-2 image, they unintentionally removed `ntpd` package in favor of a systemd-timesyncd config. some VMs didn't pick up timesync early on boot; edges showed drift.

samir_oncall: temporary workaround: we've kicked relevant nodes for a swift re-provision (reboot + timesync). Also we left handshake threshold relaxed for 15 mins.

customer-ops: cust-338 confirms improvement: streaming spinner resolved, occasional 5-10s pauses for long streams only. they've paused escalation but want RCA.

ajay_runtime: RCA notes to collect: - why timesync not initialized on these nodes - why handshake uses strict drift check together with autoscaler (we should degrade more gracefully) - why streaming sessions experienced tokenization stalls when pool scale changes (KV cache eviction?).

maria_sre: collecting perf traces and KV cache metrics. suspect warmup path: new nodes didn't pre-warm the model KV cache; when autoscaler added nodes quickly, first requests hit cold KV path causing tail latency. combined with inflight stream resumption leads to p99 spikes.

samir_oncall: open action items: 1) infra to patch AMI to ensure timesync enabled and tested (nora) 2) runtime to add graceful handshake fallback and allow autoscaler to queue warmup tasks (ajay) 3) SRE to add runbook steps for temporarily relaxing handshake threshold and forced scale (maria) 4) product to communicate customer RCA (nora/customer-ops).

nora_prodeng: acknowledged. I'll schedule infra patch and coordinate customer communication template.

maria_sre: adding notes to postmortem: customer impact: ~3 customers, percentage of requests over SLO during incident window (~10:05-10:30 UTC) = 3.2% of total dedicated requests in us-west-2; top p99 = 42s at peak; streaming stall sessions ~120 sessions impacted.

ajay_runtime: followups: - consider relaxing strict drift rejection in favor of a warning + allow one-time handshake for autoscaler candidates - implement pre-warm hook for new nodes to load KV cache before marking healthy.

samir_oncall: handing off to next shift — paged @maria_sre and @ajay_runtime for follow-up post-mortem. leaving incident thread pinned.

incident-bot: Incident auto-summary created: #INC-2026-0315-01 — Dedicated autoscale handshake time drift caused delayed pool expansion => queue spike => streaming tail latency breach. Assigned owners: infra(nora), runtime(ajay), sre(maria).

maria_sre: thanks team. will update postmortem doc and link once drafted. Closing on-call thread but keeping monitoring until metrics stable for 2 hours.

samir_oncall: 10:29 UTC — all immediate mitigations done. continuing RCA.

nora_prodeng: 10:45 UTC — infra patch staged to us-west-2 AMI; will roll to prod tomorrow with verification.

ajay_runtime: 11:00 UTC — pushed ticket to runtime backlog for handshake fallback + pre-warm, ETA 2 weeks.

customer-ops: 11:10 UTC — notified impacted customers with interim explanation and mitigation summary.

maria_sre: 11:25 UTC — monitoring shows p99 trending back to baseline. marking incident as mitigated. will file postmortem and link here.
